answer: A new agent begins on a bare knoll: a hollow credential with no history, allowed only trivial tasks. Each job it completes is checked by independent peers, and a signed receipt is appended to its record, like a plume added to a cap. Privileges unlock only as receipts accumulate, so a Sybil operator must pay the full cost of doing real, verified work for every fake identity, while an honest agent earns access once and keeps it. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a hundred working histories is not.
